results.title: Continental will pass on tariff costs – CFO - Just Auto
results.content:
Automakers in the US face potential disruption from the impact of tariffs on North America’s highly integrated industry and there are fears that the higher costs in the supply chain and for finished vehicles could lead to much higher prices for US consumers. There is also much uncertainty over the duration and detail of the new tariffs and how they will be applied to automotive components that cross NA borders.

Email newsletter icon

### Sign up for our daily news round-up! [...] Find out more

The company’s CFO, Olaf Schick, told Bloomberg that it cannot absorb additional duties in the US. ““For us it’s clear: We cannot bear additional duties, and we are informing our customers about that,” he told the news agency.

Continental has also set up a tariffs task force and is talking to customers in North America who are receiving its Mexico sourced products, the report said. [...] Bloomberg noted that Continental operates more than twenty plants in Mexico and generates around a fifth of its group sales in the US.

This week the US President has announced new 25% tariffs on imports from Canada and Mexico as well as a 20% tariff on imports from China.
